72	*
73	*********************************************************************
74	*
75	* PURPOSE    : Evaluate position, first derivative, curvature and radius of
76	*              curvature of a curve at a given parameter value, from the
77	*              left hand side.
78	*
79	*
80	*
81	* INPUT      : curve    - Pointer to the curve for which position
82	*                       and derivatives are to be computed.
83	*              der      - The number of derivatives to compute.
84	*                       < 0 : Error.
85	*                       = 0 : Compute position.
86	*                       = 1 : Compute position and first derivative.
87	*                       etc.
88	*              parvalue - The parameter value at which to compute
89	*                       position and derivatives.
90	*
91	*
92	*
93	* INPUT/OUTPUT : leftknot - Pointer to the interval in the knot vector
94	*                        where ax is located. If et is the knot vector,
95	*                        the relation
96	*
97	*                          et[ileft] < parvalue <= et[ileft+1]
98	*
99	*                        should hold. (If parvalue == et[ik-1] then ileft
100	*                        should be ik-1. Here in is the number of B-spline
101	*                        coefficients.)
102	*                        If ileft does not have the right value upon
103	*                        entry to the routine, its value will be changed
104	*                        to the value satisfying the above condition.
105	*
106	*
107	*
108	* OUTPUT     : derive   - Double array of dimension [(ider+1)*idim]
109	*                       containing the position and derivative vectors.
110	*                       (idim is the number of components of each B-spline
111	*                       coefficient, i.e. the dimension of the Euclidean
112	*                       space in which the curve lies.)
113	*                       These vectors are stored in the following order:
114	*                       First the idim components of the position vector,
115	*                       then the idim components of the tangent vector,
116	*                       then the idim components of the second derivative
117	*                       vector, and so on.
118	*                       (The C declaration of eder as a two dimensional array
119	*                       would therefore be eder[ider+1,idim].)
120	*              curvature - Array of dimension idim
121	*              radius_of_curvature -  A radius of curvature =-1, indicates
122	*                       that the radius of curvature is infinit.
123	*              jstat  - Status messages
124	*                                         > 0      : Warning.
125	*                                         = 0      : Ok.
126	*                                         < 0      : Error.
127	*
128	*
129	* METHOD     : The derivatives are evaluated from the left hand
130	*              side by  s1227
131	*              The curvature and the radius of curvature are evaluated
132	*              by s1307
133	*
134	* REFERENCES :
135	*
136	*-
137	* CALLS      : s1227, s1307
138	*
139	* WRITTEN BY : Cathrine Tegnander
140	* MODIFIED BY :
141	* REVISED BY :
142	*
143	*********************************************************************
144	*/
145	{
146	  int ider=2;                 /* minimum number of derivatives needed to
147	                                 calculated the curvature */
148	  int kdim = curve -> idim;   /* copy curve attribute to local parameter */
149	  int kstat=0;                /* local status variable */
150	  int kpos = 0;               /* local error position  */
151	  int iknot = 0;              /* local version of leftknot */
152	  double *iderive = SISL_NULL;     /* pointer to array used to store the position
153	                                 and the first and second derivatives  */
154	  double *egeo = SISL_NULL;        /* pointer to store curvature and radius of
155	                                 curvature */

114	*                       First the idim components of the position vector,
115	*                       then the idim components of the tangent vector,
116	*                       then the idim components of the second derivative
117	*                       vector, and so on.
118	*                       (The C declaration of eder as a two dimensional array
119	*                       would therefore be eder[ider+1,idim].)
120	*              curvature - Array of dimension idim
121	*              radius_of_curvature -  A radius of curvature =-1, indicates
122	*                       that the radius of curvature is infinit.
123	*              jstat  - Status messages
124	*                                         > 0      : Warning.
125	*                                         = 0      : Ok.
126	*                                         < 0      : Error.
127	*
128	*
129	* METHOD     : The derivatives are evaluated from the right hand
130	*              side by  s1221
131	*              The curvature and the radius of curvature are evaluated
132	*              by s1307
133	*
134	* REFERENCES :
135	*
136	*-
137	* CALLS      : s1221, s1307
138	*
139	* WRITTEN BY : Cathrine Tegnander
140	* MODIFIED BY :
141	* REVISED BY :
142	*
143	*********************************************************************
144	*/
145	{
146	  int ider=2;                 /* minimum number of derivatives needed to
147	                                 calculated the curvature */
148	  int kdim = curve -> idim;   /* copy curve attribute to local parameter */
149	  int kstat=0;                /* local status variable */
150	  int kpos = 0;               /* local error position  */
151	  int iknot = 0;              /* local version of leftknot */
152	  double *iderive = SISL_NULL;     /* pointer to array used to store the position
153	                                 and the first and second derivatives  */
154	  double *egeo = SISL_NULL;        /* pointer to store curvature and radius of
155	                                 curvature */
156	
157	  iderive= newarray(3*kdim,DOUBLE);
158	  if (iderive == SISL_NULL)
159	    goto err101;
160	  egeo= newarray(3*kdim+1,DOUBLE);
161	  if (egeo == SISL_NULL)
162	    goto err101;
163	
164	
165	  /* Evaluate the derivatives */
166	    if (der<2)
167	      {
168		s1221(curve,ider,parvalue,&iknot,iderive,&kstat);
169		if (kstat<0) goto error;
170	
171		/* Copy position */
172		memcopy(derive,iderive,(der+1)*kdim,DOUBLE);
173	      }
174	  else
175	    {
176	      s1221(curve,der,parvalue,&iknot,derive,&kstat);
177	      if (kstat<0) goto error;
178	
179	      	/* Copy position */
180		memcopy(iderive,derive,3*kdim,DOUBLE);
181	    }
182	    *leftknot = iknot;
183	
184	  /* Evaluate the curvature and the radius_of_curvature */
185	  s1307(iderive,kdim,egeo,&kstat);
186	  if (kstat<0) goto error;
187	
188	  /* Copy position */
189	  memcopy(curvature,egeo+kdim*2,kdim,DOUBLE);
190	
191	  *radius_of_curvature = egeo[kdim*3];
192	
193	  /* Free memory */
194	 freearray(iderive);
195	 freearray(egeo);
196	
197	 /* Successful computations.  */
198	
199	  *jstat = 0;
200	  goto out;
201	
202	  /* Error in scratch allocation */
203	 err101:
204	  *jstat = -101;
205	  s6err("s1226",*jstat,kpos);
206	
207	  /* Error in lower level routine.  */
208	
209	 error:  *jstat = kstat;
210	  s6err("S1226",*jstat,kpos);
211	  goto out;
212	
213	 out: return;
214	
215	}

  int *left_obj_2;		/* Pretopology information, one for each

typedef struct SISLTrack
{
  SISLSurf *psurf_1;		/* Pointer to first surface in intersection */
  SISLSurf *psurf_2;		/* Pointer to second surface in intersection */

  SISLCurve *pcurve_2d_1;	/* Pointer to 2D support curve in first
				   parameter space. */
  SISLCurve *pcurve_2d_2;	/* Pointer to 2D support curve in second
				   parameter space. */

				    = 0, Bspline vs Bspline

				= 1001 Bspline vs Torus surface

				  projection

				  projection
				= 1005 Bspline silhouette line, circular
			          projection */

  double eimpli[16];		/* Description of the implicit surface */
  int turned;			/* Connection between the direction of the
				   support curve and the cross product
				   between the two surface normals.

  int pretop[4];		/* Pretopology */
  int sing_start;               /* Singular start end point markers */
  int sing_end;
} SISLTrack;

/* This file contains the description of a list connecting points that
   belong to an intersection curve.                                    */

typedef struct SISLIntlist
{
  SISLIntpt *pfirst;		/* Pointer to first point in list. */
  SISLIntpt *plast;		/* Pointer to last point in list.  */
  int ind_first;		/* Index pointer in pfirst         */
  int ind_last;			/* Index pointer in plast          */
  int itype;			/* Status of curve-segment.
                               = 0 : open curve, no singularities.
                               = 1 : closed curve, no singularities.
                               = 2 : more than two curves meet at start point.
                               = 3 : more than two curves meet at end point.
                               = 4 : more than two curves meet at start
                                     and end point.
                               = 5 : isolated singularity.
                               = 6 : touching area of surface.            */
  int inumb;			/* Number of points in the list.          */
  int pretop[4];		/* Pretopology */
} SISLIntlist;

#define DEQUAL(a,b) \
  ( (fabs((a) - (b)) <= (REL_PAR_RES * MAX(MAX(fabs(a),fabs(b)),(double)1.0))) ? (1) : (0) )
